### Job summary

Vintage Modern is seeking a Head of Operations to lead all aspects of manufacturing operations in Buford, GA. You will own the master build schedule, manage headcount and allocation by station, and ensure all departments align with policy and expectations to deliver quality, on-time vehicles daily.

You will coach production managers and leaders, build a culture of accountability, implement process improvements, and drive safety, 5S, and continuous improvement across the plant.

### Responsibilities

- Own the master build schedule and adherence to it.
- Own all manpower planning: headcount, staffing and allocation by station, line and department.
- Ensure every department under you is compliant with company policy and expectations.
- Coach the coaches and develop production managers, supervisors and group leads into accountable leaders.
- Set clear authority and measurable expectations at every level and ensure decisions are handled at the right level.
- Get the right people on the bus, across production, warehouse and procurement.
- Identify talent internally and with People and Culture on recruiting as the company scales.
- Build a succession plan for every key operations role.

Head of Operations

All Full Time Buford, GA, US

2 days ago Requisition ID: 1004

**Delivery and Build Quality**

- Own production of all product lines, and the outcome: every vehicle built correctly, on time, every time, with world-class quality.
- Ensure every station, including pre-assembly, finishes on time every day, across every product line.
- Enforce that no defect passes its process and no vehicle moves to the next station with an open action. No defect is left open in iAuditor at the end of the day.
- Ensure the nonconformance process is followed every day, and that rework is coordinated, completed correctly and on time, and logged.
- Ensure vehicle shipments are scheduled to the day and every vehicle ships on time.
- Partner with Quality, Engineering and Program Management on new product launches, including the Fastback.
- **Build quality into the process.** Partner with Quality and Engineering to set clear acceptance criteria and checkpoints at every station, so no vehicle reaches final inspection with a defect and reliance on final inspection falls.

**Planning and Scheduling**

- Own the master build schedule, and adherence to it.
- Own all manpower planning: headcount, staffing and allocation by station, line and department, ahead of demand.
- Ensure every department under you is compliant with company policy and expectations.

**Leadership, Talent and Succession**

- **Coach the coaches.** Develop production managers, supervisors and group leads into leaders who drive accountability through their own teams.
- Set clear authority and measurable expectations at every level, so decisions and problems are handled at the right level, not escalated by default.
- Get the right people on the bus, the wrong people off the bus, and the right people in the right seats, across production, warehouse and procurement.
- Identify talent, internally and externally, and partner with People and Culture on recruiting as the company scales.
- Build a succession plan for every key operations role, so the organization never depends on one person.
- Create leverage through people: set extremely high expectations and build a team that meets them without you in the room.

**Accountability and Operating System**

- **Own who owns what by when.** Every operational priority, problem and commitment has a defined outcome, one accountable owner and a firm due date, and is tracked to verified completion.
- Maintain a clear, reliable view of priorities, owners, due dates and progress. Intervene early when results are at risk, and drive recovery plans to completion.
- **Lead the operational transformation.** Assess current performance, identify the constraints limiting results, and execute a prioritized improvement plan with measurable outcomes and firm milestones.
- Assess the existing operating systems, decide where they need to improve, and build the plan to level them up.
- Establish the processes and systems that create a safe, efficient, high-quality work environment, and make sure they are followed every single day.
- Serve as an expert-level problem solver at every level, from a single station to the whole operation. Find root causes, implement corrective actions, **verify they worked**, and build the lessons into processes and training so problems are solved permanently.
- Set the daily operating cadence: team lead reports reviewed daily, issues acted on and escalated properly, and drift caught in hours, not weeks.
- Ensure every employee is trained to their tasks and follows company SOPs and work instructions.

**Safety, 5S and Continuous Improvement**

- Own plant safety. PPE and safety standards are followed every day, without exception.
- Own organization and 5S: standards set, enforced and personally audited; every station has the tools it needs and only what it needs.
- Drive continuous improvement, efficiency and scalability across every station.
- Improve flow: remove bottlenecks, balance workloads across stations, improve how material is presented at the station, and eliminate wasted effort.
- Own vehicle protection standards and on-task discipline across the floor.

**Warehouse, Inventory Storage and Procurement**

- Own the warehouse and inventory storage, including inventory control, so material flows from receiving through delivery to the station without interruption.
- Hold the Warehouse Manager accountable for receiving, storage, inventory accuracy, controlled material transactions and reliable delivery of the correct parts to production.
- Hold the Procurement Manager accountable for purchasing execution, supplier delivery, lead-time management, cost control and fast resolution of material shortages, including supplier readiness for new product lines.
- Ensure procurement, warehouse and production work from one coordinated plan.
- Ensure inventory accuracy and that material shortages never stop a station.
- Identify supply chain risks early, from long-lead parts to single-source suppliers, and put mitigation in place before they become shortages.

**Reporting and Metrics**

- Report first pass yield, on-time delivery, scrap cost, safety and station efficiency.
- Maintain a capacity-versus-demand and resource allocation plan, with headcount and cost tracking, and show what is being done to maximize efficiency.
- Track planned versus actual labor and material performance to improve productivity and control costs.
- Give the COO accurate performance reporting, early visibility into risks and actionable recommendations, and know when and why to escape.
- Report monthly on team performance, including top performers, bottom performers and highest-risk employees.

## Job description

Position Title: Director, Regulated Manufacturing Transformation

Location: Multiple U.S. Locations  
Work Authorization: U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident Required

Position Overview

An established technology and engineering solutions organization is seeking a senior industry leader to drive growth, innovation, and strategic client engagement within highly regulated manufacturing sectors.

This role combines commercial leadership, industry expertise, digital transformation consulting, and executive relationship management. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in expanding market presence, developing industry-focused solutions, and helping organizations modernize manufacturing operations while maintaining regulatory compliance.

Key Responsibilities

Industry Leadership & Market Development

• Establish and execute long-term growth strategies for regulated manufacturing sectors.  
• Monitor emerging industry trends, regulatory developments, and technology innovations.  
• Serve as a trusted advisor to executive stakeholders across manufacturing organizations.  
• Represent the organization at industry forums, conferences, and executive briefings.  
• Develop strategic insights, industry perspectives, and market-facing thought leadership content.  
• Guide clients through modernization initiatives involving manufacturing operations, quality systems, and digital transformation.

Solution Strategy & Innovation

• Design industry-focused service offerings spanning manufacturing technology, automation, data platforms, analytics, and operational excellence.  
• Partner with technical and delivery teams to create scalable solutions and reusable frameworks.  
• Develop business cases, value propositions, and go-to-market strategies for new offerings.  
• Support development of solution architectures involving manufacturing systems, industrial data environments, cloud technologies, and advanced analytics.

Business Growth & Client Engagement

• Lead strategic business development initiatives within regulated manufacturing accounts.  
• Build and expand relationships with senior executives and operational leaders.  
• Identify, qualify, and pursue transformational consulting and technology opportunities.  
• Guide complex proposal development, commercial negotiations, and contract discussions.  
• Contribute to revenue growth through expansion of existing relationships and acquisition of new clients.  
• Present business value, operational improvements, compliance benefits, and ROI to executive audiences.

Leadership & Collaboration

• Mentor business development and client-facing teams.  
• Collaborate with engineering, automation, software, analytics, and consulting groups.  
• Support major client engagements as an executive sponsor and strategic advisor.  
• Foster alignment between business objectives, regulatory requirements, and technical delivery.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Technology, or a related discipline.  
• 12+ years of experience within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or similarly regulated manufacturing environments.  
• Demonstrated success leading strategic client relationships and revenue-generating initiatives.  
• Experience selling or delivering large-scale consulting, automation, manufacturing technology, or digital transformation programs.  
• Strong understanding of compliance-driven manufacturing environments and industry regulations.  
• Experience engaging executive-level stakeholders and influencing strategic decisions.  
• Proven ability to drive sustainable business growth and market expansion.

Preferred Expertise

Experience in several of the following areas:

• Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES)  
• Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM)  
• Industrial Automation  
• Operational Technology (OT)  
• Industrial Data Platforms  
• SCADA and Visualization Systems  
• Cloud-Based Manufacturing Solutions  
• Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence  
• Quality and Compliance Systems  
• Systems Integration

Ideal Candidate Profile

The successful candidate is a strategic business leader who combines:

• Deep knowledge of regulated manufacturing industries  
• Commercial growth and client acquisition expertise  
• Digital transformation consulting experience  
• Strong executive presence and communication skills  
• Ability to connect business strategy with technology execution

Additional Information

• Travel requirement of approximately 40%.  
• Exceptional presentation, communication, and relationship-building skills required.  
• Must be authorized to work permanently in the United States without sponsorship.  
• Candidates from direct competitor organizations may not be considered.

### Description

**Job Summary:** The Director of Manufacturing Engineering is the overall department leader for  
Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and Continuous Improvement across the manufacturing organization. Reporting to the VP of Manufacturing, this role establishes and executes the strategy, standards, systems, and talent required to translate product designs into safe, repeatable, efficient, and scalable manufacturing processes. The Director leads two integrated teams: (1) Manufacturing Engineering and  
Industrial Engineering, responsible for EBOM-to-MBOM transformation, manufacturing product structures, Methods of Manufacture, routings, work instructions, plant layouts, digital twin simulations, equipment capacity models, tooling, equipment, and machinery; and (2) Continuous Improvement, responsible for Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen events, 5S, Lean manufacturing initiatives, standard work, and structured problem solving. The role partners closely with Manufacturing Operations across several value streams, Product Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Planning, Facilities, and EHS to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and manufacturing readiness while  
supporting new product introductions, capacity expansion, and growth across multiple manufacturing locations. **Minimum Qualifications: (Education, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills):** * Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering,  
  Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, operational excellence, or manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years of leading technical teams.
* Demonstrated experience leading Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial  
  Engineering, and/or Continuous Improvement functions in a complex

_El Segundo, California | On-site_

This role builds the manufacturing function from today's flight prototypes to a production line that delivers interceptors at volume. You will own how the hardware gets built, including the facility, processes, tooling, quality, and the team doing the work. You will report to the CEO.

Interceptors only matter if they can be produced reliably, affordably, and in quantity. You will partner with the founders, engineering leads, and supply chain to ensure the vehicle is designed for manufacture and can be built at the rate and cost customers require.

We are a seed-stage, venture-backed defense technology company building affordable, modular interceptors for air and missile defense, with surface-launched and space-based platforms in development. * Build and lead the manufacturing team, hiring technicians and manufacturing engineers as the company grows

* Own manufacturing safety, including safe handling and storage of energetic materials
* Ensure manufacturing meets customer, contract, and regulatory requirements

* Low-rate initial production on defense programs
* Lean manufacturing, automation, or high-volume production
* ERP or MES implementation
* Prior early-stage startup experience

**Why Join Us**

* Build the manufacturing organization and facility from the ground up
* Report directly to the CEO with a seat in core company decisions
* Shape the path from prototype to production for a defense product
* Hire and lead your own team
* Early equity in a seed-stage company with a rapidly growing team
* Mission with direct national security impact

**Compensation Details**

$170,000 - $210,000 + equity

## Job description

Description The Director of Manufacturing leads Fortem’s day-to-day manufacturing operations, with accountability for production execution, inventory control, warehouse operations, and manufacturing systems across multiple product lines. This role improves throughput, schedule attainment, productivity, and lead times while maintaining safe operations and product quality.

Reporting to the VP, Manufacturing and Operations, the Director develops manufacturing leaders, establishes consistent operating practices, and translates delivery priorities into executable production plans. The Director partners with Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, and Program Management to resolve constraints and prepare manufacturing operations for continued growth.

The Director is accountable for measurable manufacturing performance and for building a scalable operating organization that consistently delivers against customer, quality, cost, and schedule commitments.

**Key Responsibilities**

Manufacturing Leadership Manage and develop production managers and operational leaders through clear expectations, coaching, performance management, and succession planning. Establish consistent standard work, operating routines, and accountability across manufacturing and warehouse teams. Provide the VP and cross-functional stakeholders with manufacturing forecasts, risks, and recovery plans; communicate delivery impacts early and recommend actions.

Build a scalable manufacturing organization by developing production managers, establishing clear ownership and decision-making authority, and ensuring teams consistently meet safety, quality, cost, and delivery objectives. Production Execution & Continuous Improvement Translate delivery requirements into coordinated production plans, staffing requirements, and operating targets.

Own schedule attainment and throughput; lead operating reviews, resolve competing priorities, and direct recovery actions. Lead improvements that reduce bottlenecks, work-in-progress delays, material shortages, and rework to improve productivity and shorten lead times. Monitor safety, quality, delivery, throughput, labor productivity, inventory accuracy, work in progress, and lead time; verify that improvements produce sustained results.

Establish and achieve measurable manufacturing performance targets, using data-driven operating reviews to identify performance gaps, assign corrective actions, and sustain improvements. Inventory, Warehouse & Manufacturing Systems Oversee receiving, storage, kitting, production replenishment, material movement, and shipment preparation to maintain efficient material flow.

Maintain inventory accuracy through disciplined transactions, cycle counting, and reconciliation with Finance and Supply Chain. Ensure accurate, timely use of ERP and manufacturing systems for work orders, inventory records, production status, and operational reporting. Partner with Engineering, Quality Assurance, and Supply Chain to maintain accurate manufacturing documentation and material requirements and control product and process changes.

Ensure production plans are executable based on material availability, labor capacity, and equipment constraints, and maintain disciplined ERP execution to provide accurate visibility into production status, shortages, and projected completion dates. Quality & Safety Maintain manufacturing accountability for quality at the source; support defect containment, root-cause investigations, and corrective actions to reduce scrap and rework.

Reinforce safety, housekeeping, and process compliance, ensuring production demands do not bypass required inspections, approvals, or safe work practices. Maintain clear boundaries with Quality Assurance, preserving its independent authority for inspection, product acceptance, and quality-system compliance while ensuring manufacturing promptly addresses defects and corrective actions.

Financial Management & Capacity Readiness Manage manufacturing expenses and labor performance within approved budgets; identify cost drivers and implement productivity improvements. Drive cost and productivity improvements by monitoring labor utilization, cost per unit, scrap, rework, and other significant operating cost drivers.

Assess capacity and staffing needs; recommend hiring, cross-training, equipment, facility, and capital investments to the VP. Lead manufacturing readiness for new or revised products and expanded production areas, coordinating staffing, training, tooling, materials, and documented processes. Develop and execute manufacturing capacity plans covering production layout, staffing models, equipment utilization, material flow, and facility readiness to support forecasted demand and business growth Requirements Required Skills & Qualifications 10+ years of progressive manufacturing or operations experience, including at least 5 years in leadership roles managing managers or multiple operational teams.

Experience leading production across multiple product lines in a hardware or technical manufacturing environment. Experience overseeing inventory control, warehouse operations, and material flow. Demonstrated results improving throughput, schedule attainment, productivity, and manufacturing lead times. Strong working knowledge of ERP systems, work-order control, inventory transactions, and manufacturing reporting.

Experience developing production leaders and establishing consistent operating practices during organizational growth. Working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, capacity planning, root-cause problem-solving, and quality improvement. Strong financial and analytical skills, including labor planning, budgeting, cost analysis, and productivity measurement.

Ability to resolve competing priorities and collaborate with Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, and Program Management. Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, engineering, operations, business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant education, training, and experience.

**Preferred Skills**

Experience in aerospace, defense, unmanned aircraft systems, robotics, or complex electromechanical manufacturing. Experience scaling operations through facility expansion, new product introductions, or substantial production growth. Experience implementing or improving ERP, manufacturing execution, warehouse management, or production reporting systems.

Familiarity with ISO 9001, AS9100, or comparable quality management systems and controlled manufacturing practices. Experience in mixed-volume manufacturing with changing product configurations. Lean or Six Sigma certification; APICS/ASCM CPIM, CSCP, or comparable operations credentials. Master’s degree in business, engineering, operations, or a related field.

Fortem Technologies is the global leader in airspace security, delivering advanced solutions that protect against today’s autonomous aerial threats while ensuring the safety of tomorrow’s advanced air mobility. Fortem’s AI-powered Sky. Dome® Family of Systems combines True. View™ sensors, command-and-control software, and autonomous Drone.

Hunter® interceptors to defend military, government, and commercial operations worldwide from hostile or unauthorized drones. Fortem is the only company authorized to deploy a drone-on-drone kinetic interceptor in U.S. airspace, and its technology has been validated in operational deployments across Europe, the Middle East, and East Asia.

Headquartered in Lindon, Utah, Fortem is privately held and backed by Lockheed Martin, DCVC, Toshiba, AE Industrial Partners, AIM13, Signia Venture Partners, and others. Fortem Technologies is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

We do not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable laws. **About the Role**

Our company is actively executing a focused M&A strategy with specific target acquisitions designed to expand market share and capture operational synergies. To support this growth, implementation of a standardized enterprise operating platform is already underway across both existing locations, including ERP and HR software standardization.

The Director of Operations will own the ongoing execution and continuous refinement of this platform—ensuring seamless adoption, sustaining floor-level discipline, and refining our operational playbook so that future target acquisitions can be rapidly integrated into our standardized tech stack and operating framework.

* **Visible Leadership & Travel:** Travel regularly between Decatur, AL and Watertown, SD—as well as future acquisition sites as our footprint expands—to maintain a visible shop-floor presence, conduct operational audits, align site cultures, and ensure consistent platform adoption.
